paper_sections.title: Brain Reactivity to Smoking Cues Prior to Smoking Cessation Predicts Ability to Maintain Tobacco Abstinence
Region-of-Interest (ROI) Analyses: Relation to Smoking Cessation Outcome and Emotional Stroop Performance
Correlations Between FMRI and Emotional Stroop Data

description.value: The study examined whether prequit fMRI reactivity to smoking-related images and attentional bias to smoking-related words could identify nicotine-dependent women who would later slip during a smoking cessation attempt.

design.value: Prospective observational prediction study nested within an 8-week smoking cessation clinical trial. Twenty-one nicotine-dependent women underwent prequit fMRI during smoking-related and neutral image viewing and were tested on an emotional Stroop task before quitting; participants were subsequently grouped according to whether they smoked after attaining at least 24 hours of abstinence.

description.value: A measure used to characterize nicotine dependence severity.

Smoking-related and neutral words, matched for length and use frequency, were displayed in colored fonts; subjects reported word color as quickly and accurately as possible while ignoring word meaning. Reaction times and accuracies were recorded.
Expired air CO was measured at screening and weekly during smoking cessation; subjects reporting abstinence with expired CO <9 ppmv were considered abstinent.
Baseline smoking behavior was characterized by recording and measuring pack-years of tobacco smoking.
Weekly self-report of smoking behavior in the prior 7 days was obtained using the Timeline Followback Method.

description.value: Twenty-one women underwent neuroimaging at McLean Hospital before participating in a smoking cessation clinical trial at Massachusetts General Hospital.

reported smoking ≥10 cigarettes per day in the previous 6 months

exclusion_criteria.value: alcohol use disorder in the prior 6 months

recruitment_method.value: Subjects underwent neuroimaging at McLean Hospital before participating in a smoking cessation clinical trial at Massachusetts General Hospital.

clinical_characteristics.value: Subjects reported smoking ≥10 cigarettes per day in the previous 6 months; baseline smoking behavior was characterized by pack-years, expiratory CO levels, the number of cigarettes smoked the morning before imaging, and FTND scores.

medication_status.value: Smoking was not restricted until shortly before imaging. After prequit imaging, participants received nicotine patch (21 mg/day for 4 weeks, 14 mg/day for 2 weeks, 7 mg/day for 2 weeks) and 2-mg nicotine polacrilex gum or lozenge, up to 12 mg/day, as needed.

clinical_characteristics.value: Slips took place on average 17.4 days (range: 1–49 days) after established abstinence.

medication_status.value: Subjects slipped while on nicotine replacement therapy.

task_description.value: During fMRI, subjects viewed smoking-related or neutral images. Animal images were shown to prompt subjects to press a response button and were included to ensure subjects attended to stimuli but were not used in data analyses.

design_type.value: six equal-length blocks with pseudo-randomized image presentation

stimuli.value: Smoking-related images showed people smoking, hands holding cigarettes, or cigarettes alone; neutral images had general content matched to the smoking images but no smoking cues; animal images were also presented.

task_performance_measures.value: Response button presses to animal images

task_description.value: Smoking-related and neutral words, matched for length and use frequency in the English language, were displayed in red, green, or blue fonts. After a 96-trial practice block of letter strings, four 33-trial experimental blocks separated by 5-sec breaks were run in the word order neutral, smoking, smoking, neutral; analyses were restricted to the first two blocks.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to report word color as quickly and accurately as possible and to ignore word meaning.

stimuli.value: Smoking-related and neutral words matched for length and use frequency in English, displayed in red, green, or blue fonts; letter strings were used for practice.

task_name.value: 8-week smoking cessation phase of the clinical trial

task_description.value: After prequit imaging and other assessments, all subjects quit smoking during the 8-week smoking cessation phase of the clinical trial.

task_performance_measures.value: Weekly self-report of smoking behavior in the prior 7 days and weekly expired CO measurements

modality.value: multiplanar rapidly acquired gradient-echo structural images

instrument.value: Siemens Trio 3 Tesla scanner (Erlangen, Germany) with a circularly polarized head coil

description.value: Multiplanar rapidly acquired gradient-echo structural images were acquired with TR = 2.1 sec, TE = 2.7 msec, 128 slices, 256 × 256 matrix, flip angle = 12°, and resolution = 1.0 × 1.0 × 1.33 mm.

instrument.value: Siemens Trio 3 Tesla scanner (Erlangen, Germany) with a circularly polarized head coil

description.value: Gradient echo echo-planar images were acquired with TR = 2 sec, TE = 30 msec, 64 × 64 matrix, field of view = 224, flip angle = 75°, 30 slices, and 3.5 mm isotropic resolution with 0 mm gap.

Images were slice-time corrected, motion corrected, spatially smoothed, resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm isotropic voxels, and spatially normalized into Talairach space. A program based on Lemieux et al. modeled out time points exhibiting motion >1.75 mm.

software.value: program based on Lemieux et al.

steps.value: spatial smoothing with a 6-mm Gaussian kernel
modeling out time points exhibiting motion >1.75 mm

model_settings.value: Image regressors for smoking, neutral, and animal images and motion confound regressors were included; the HRF was convolved with square waves defined by the onset–offset of each image presentation. Beta maps comparing smoking with neutral images were created for each subject.

Subject-level smoking versus neutral beta maps were used to compare fMRI activity between slip and abstinent subject groups. Multiple comparisons were corrected at the cluster level using Monte Carlo simulation; the selected cluster extent was 31 three-mm resampled isotropic voxels, approximately 837 mm3, yielding p = .005.

Beta weights for smoking image > neutral image contrasts were extracted from the anterior insula, dACC, DLPFC, and amygdala and averaged across all voxels within each ROI. Insula and amygdala ROIs were defined anatomically; DLPFC and dACC were defined on the basis of the functional connectivity analysis.

Analyses were run separately on accuracy and reaction-time scores, entering Group (slip, abstinent) as a between-subject factor, Condition (neutral versus smoking-related words) as a repeated measure, and FTND scores as covariates.
Pearson's correlation coefficient was calculated to evaluate relationships between ROI fMRI activation and emotional Stroop task performance.
Emotional Stroop interference effects were tested as predictors of mean insular and dACC activity after controlling for FTND scores.

A leave-one-out cross-validation strategy was used, in which each case was iteratively classified on the basis of all other cases. Predictors included Stroop interference reaction time and accuracy effects, mean anterior insula fMRI reactivity, and dACC fMRI reactivity.

A principal-component analysis data reduction step was used, all data were concatenated into a matrix, and group spatial ICA was performed. The GIFT minimum description length algorithm determined that 25 optimal components existed; Component Number 2 containing bilateral insula and anterior cingulate was selected.

Each participant's Component Number 2 time course was converted into a Brain Voyager-compatible regressor, and a random effects GLM containing the component time course and motion confound regressors was run. The Component Number 2 activation map was Bonferroni corrected to p < .01 and compared between slip and abstinence subjects.

definition.value: Greater smoking-related versus neutral image reactivity in the slip group relative to the abstinent group

voxelwise_threshold_type.value: individual voxel Type 1 error of p

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-level correction using a Monte Carlo simulation

model_representation_notes.value: The GLM used a 2-gamma hemodynamic response function convolved with square waves defined by the onset–offset of each image presentation.

interpretations.value: Slip subjects had heightened fMRI reactivity to smoking-related images in brain regions implicated in emotion, interoceptive awareness, and motor planning and execution.
